---
title: Home
---

This example shows **responsive navbar text**: each item in the navbar
above can show different text at different window widths. Resize the
browser window and watch the labels change.

A navbar item's `text:` is usually a string. Here, most items give a
map from breakpoint names to text instead:

```yaml
- href: guide/index.qmd
  text:
    xs: Getting Started   # collapsed menu, below 992px
    lg: Start             # expanded but cramped, 992px to 1200px
    xl: Getting Started   # 1200px and wider
```

Each variant applies from its breakpoint up to the next key in the
map. The breakpoints are Bootstrap's:

| key | applies from |
|---|---|
| `xs` | 0 |
| `sm` | 576px |
| `md` | 768px |
| `lg` | 992px |
| `xl` | 1200px |
| `xxl` | 1400px |

## What each width shows

| window width | navbar |
|---|---|
| below 992px | collapsed menu: Getting Started, Configuration Guide, Tutorials and Examples, Release Notes, API, Community Resources, GitHub |
| 992px to 1200px | Start, Config, Tutorials, Releases, API, Community, GitHub icon only |
| 1200px to 1400px | Getting Started, Configuration Guide, Tutorials and Examples, Release Notes, API, Community, GitHub icon only |
| 1400px and wider | Getting Started, Configuration Guide, Tutorials and Examples, Release Notes, API Reference, Community, GitHub |

The short variants matter between 992px and 1200px. At 1000px, the
full labels don't fit on one line and the navbar items wrap; the short
labels fit with room to spare.

See the [guide](guide/index.qmd) for the rules in detail.
